origins: This belief often starts early. A child who is criticized, compared, ignored, teased, or treated as a problem can conclude, “The trouble must be me.” Painful experiences such as abuse, rejection, divorce, or a parent’s anger can leave the same message, because children tend to blame themselves for what adults do. Later, every mistake, struggle, or difference seems to confirm it. Over time the feeling of being “broken” or “not like other people” can settle in so deeply that it feels like a fact rather than a belief.
teaches: Scripture is honest that every person is affected by sin and lives in a broken world. But the Bible never says that you are uniquely defective or that you are the one thing God got wrong. You were made in God’s image. The psalmist praised God because he was fearfully and wonderfully made. In Christ, there is now no condemnation, and anyone in Him is a new creation. Struggles, weaknesses, and scars are real, and some deserve care and help, but they are things you have, not the whole of who you are. God knows you completely and still calls you His workmanship.
self_statements: Other people seem normal; I am not.
If people really knew me, they would see what is wrong with me.
I always mess things up because I am broken.
Everyone else got something I was born without.
When things go wrong, it must be my fault.
I have to hide the real me.
errors: Calling my whole self “wrong” because of a struggle, a mistake, or a painful feeling.
Treating a few hard moments as proof that I am defective in every way.
Believing that because I feel broken, I must be broken.
Assuming that other people’s anger, rejection, or problems were caused by something wrong in me.
questions: What exactly do I mean by “something is wrong with me”? Can I name it?
When did I first start believing this, and who taught it to me?
Is this a struggle I have, or is it the whole of who I am?
Would I say this about a friend who had the same struggles I have?
What evidence do I have that I am loved, valued, or capable?
How does God describe the people He has made and redeemed?
truth: I have struggles, weaknesses, and wounds, like every person. But I am not a mistake. God made me in His image, knows me completely, and calls me His workmanship. My struggles are something I can work on and bring to Him; they are not the final word about who I am.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
Having a struggle does not make me defective.
What was done to me does not define me.
God knows me fully and still loves me.
I can grow without first proving I am worth it.
In Christ, there is no condemnation for me.
log: When the “something is wrong with me” feeling came
Each day, write down one moment when you felt broken or different. Write what happened, what you told yourself, and one more accurate statement.
actions: Separate the struggle from the self.
Write the belief as “I am…”. Then rewrite it as “I have…” or “I struggle with…”. Notice how the second version feels.
Collect the other side of the evidence.
Ask one trusted person to tell you two good things they see in you. Write them down and read them, even if you do not believe them yet.
Let one safe person see a little more of you.
Share one small, honest thing about yourself with a trusted friend, family member, or church member. Notice whether they turn away or stay.
Get help for what is real.
If something truly needs attention, such as a health concern, a habit, or a painful memory, take one step toward help this week: a doctor, pastor, or counselor.
tracker: A moment I did not feel broken
prayer: Lord, You formed me and You know me completely. When I feel broken or different, remind me that I am Your workmanship and not a mistake. Help me separate my struggles from who I am, bring my wounds to You for healing, and receive the love You have already given me in Christ. Amen.
